author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Hundreds of Mattapan residents packed a listening session Thursday to raise concerns about a proposed redesign of Blue Hill Avenue. The Boston and MBTA plan would put dedicated bus lanes in the center of the street, with riders crossing general traffic lanes to reach median boarding areas.

Opponents at Morning Star Baptist Church focused on pedestrian safety, access to neighborhood businesses and the effect of construction on the corridor. Some speakers asked officials to consider alternatives, including a long-discussed extension of the Orange Line, rather than commit to the center-running layout.

Mayor Michelle Wu and MBTA General Manager Phillip Eng attended the session. Wu said the design remains in progress and can change as public feedback is collected. The meeting was the first of four community sessions planned over the next several weeks, leaving additional opportunities for residents to review details and respond.

The proposal aims to make bus trips more reliable on one of Boston’s busiest transit corridors. The unresolved issue is how to balance that goal with safe crossings, traffic flow and commercial access. Further design work will determine whether the city modifies station locations, lane arrangements or other street features before moving ahead.
dek: A Boston and MBTA proposal would place buses in the median, prompting questions about street crossings, businesses and other transit options.
headline: Mattapan residents question center-running Blue Hill Avenue bus lanes
